title: Al-Badi', the Incomparable Originator
hookLine: the Incomparable Originator, making without a model (2:117)
tomorrow: a whole sheep given away. why would he say it 'remains'?

cards: Saturday, Dadi's apartment, half in boxes. Amira is taping the kitchen when she finds a pillowcase under the bed, and inside it a quilt: blue squares, orange triangles, one strip cut from an old school uniform.
She asks which pattern it came from. Dadi laughs. "No pattern. I started with one square and kept going."
Amira holds it up to the window. Everything she has ever made started from a tutorial, a template, someone else's version. This came from a woman, a needle and nothing to copy.
So where does a thing come from when there was nothing before it?

teach.b: The Qur'an answers with a Name. In Surah al-Baqarah, in Pickthall's words: "The Originator of the heavens and the earth! When He decreeth a thing, He saith unto it only: Be! and it is."
The Name is Al-Badi', the Originator.
Classical explanations of the Names describe it as making without a model: no blueprint before, no earlier sky to improve on.
Dadi's quilt is the human version, and even she had cloth, thread and other quilts behind her hands. Al-Badi' had none of that. Look how short the verse keeps it.
No sketch, no second version. Be, and it is. In Arabic that command is a single short word, kun.
That's the line to tell a friend tonight: the whole sky answers to one syllable.
So Muslims say people make, and Allah originates. We arrange what was already given; He gives the first thing. Some readers find a second gift hiding here.
If the Originator copies nothing, then no person is a copy either. Not you, not the kid next to you on the bus, not any face in the long line of human faces.

how: Muslims call on Allah by His Names in du'a and remembrance; Al-Badi' is remembered with the words of 2:117, Originator of the heavens and the earth.

o: the Originator, who makes without any model
the Restorer, who mends what was broken
the Designer, who plans from an old blueprint

games.q: what's inside the Name — tap the pairs.
p: made with no pattern, from old cloth

s: Al-Badi' means Allah improved on an earlier world
the verse names Him Originator of the heavens and the earth: no model came before.
in 2:117 His command to a thing is only: Be!
"He saith unto it only: Be! and it is."
Dadi's quilt is creation in the same sense as Al-Badi's
she still had cloth and thread. people arrange what was given; He gives the first thing.

games.q: your classmate shrugs: 'i'm basically a copy of my older brother. same face, same grades.' what does today's Name give you to say?
o: some readers say: the Originator copies nothing, so no person is a copy.
fair enough; siblings come from one pattern, so the copy idea holds.
only prophets were made without precedent; the rest of us are copies.
games.why: Al-Badi' makes without a model. some readers draw the next step: no face in the human line is a copy, your classmate included.

practice: Find one thing near you that exists only once: the crack in your mug, a scar on your knuckle, the swirl of your own fingertip. Look at it for the whole sit as if it had just been made. In a way, it was.

wordCard.voice: Al-Badi'. The Originator, who makes without a model, and says to a thing only: Be.

orig.note: Arabic: the Originator, from the traditional list of the Names; the Qur'an calls Him Originator of the heavens and the earth.

carryVoice: For the road: without precedent, the heavens, the earth, and the face in your mirror. Name ninety-five, gathered.
